I was finally able to re-engineer the CSS of the animation sequences to reduce the
encoding size. This allowed me to go from 7 frames (127 animation patterns) to
9 frames (512 patterns). This breaks all prior demonstrations involving the game grid.

At least 8 frames of state within the grid were needed to add mechanics beyond basic stacking.
With two additional frames I can add a bit more to the game. This only increased the CSS by
30% but would have quadrupled the CSS with my prior (higher performance) method.

The down side is that the new animation does not perform as well as the older method. When
a very large block of cells are scheduled to animate at the same moment some will appear
in the next screen refresh leaving 1/60th of a second flicker. This is because when there are
many CSS animations to render at once browsers break them into batches and render them
on separate screen refresh cycles.

I effectively doubled the number of concurrent animations with the new encoding as a trade off
to reduce the text length of the CSS. Fortunately, the frame flicker will not normally be apparent
since smaller batches of cells will be animating and can be processed in one update cycle.

Also added bounces to the line clear drop animations. Now to resynchronize the other
effects to account for the extra frames.
